observation.visible_scene: A night-time outdoor light show projected onto a modern building consisting of a central cylindrical tower flanked by two flat rectangular wings with rows of dark window openings. The building's facade is floodlit in a saturated color, and a silhouetted crowd stands in the foreground with a single person silhouette at a console on the right edge. Bright green laser beams emanate from a glowing point at the base-center of the building, spreading outward across the frame. The camera framing of the building stays essentially fixed throughout the excerpt.
visible_changes: The laser pattern cycles through distinct configurations: a dense wide radial fan filling much of the frame (frames 1-3, 16-23, 25-28), a near-off state with the building lit but beams absent (frames 4-5, 11, 24, 29-30, 38-40), narrow V/X-shaped diagonal beams plus a vertical center beam (frames 6-10, 12-15, 31-37), and side-only beams (frame 41).
The fan pattern expands and contracts radially from the same base emitter point rather than translating across the scene.
The building's floodlight color shifts from blue (frames 1-19, 29-41) to magenta/purple (frames 20-28) and back toward blue, independent of the beam pattern.
A small bright dot appears near the top-right of the building in some frames (e.g., 5, 20) and not others.
The crowd silhouette and the right-side performer silhouette remain in the same positions throughout; no clear crowd or performer motion is visible.
outside_clip_unknowns: The control source or mechanism generating the laser patterns and color changes is not shown.
What precedes frame 1 and follows frame 41 is unknown; the excerpt begins and ends mid-pattern.
Whether the bright dots on the building are separate fixtures or reflections cannot be determined.
uncertain_details: Camera motion is minimal/uncertain; the building's position is stable, so observed changes are attributed to the light show rather than to panning.
The exact origin device of the beams at the base is obscured by haze and brightness.
Distinguishing the small top dots as reflections versus independent lights is not resolvable from the frames.
